title: Second BTC trade: post-CASE-001 learning chain into CPI reclaim long
scope_rule: CASE-002 does NOT begin at CPI. Its context begins immediately after CASE-001 was closed and includes the full Sep 8-11 order-flow learning sequence that produced the eventual second trade.

position.entry_proof: At 08:53 the execution screenshot displayed a 77,613.3 position line, size 0.0191 BTC and PNL +7.3764 USDT. Using fair price 77,999.5, (77,999.5 - 77,613.3) * 0.0191 = 7.3764, confirming 77,613.3 as the displayed average entry.
position.closure: NOT_CONFIRMED; screenshot still showed an open position and a Close action. Do not mark the exchange position closed until owner confirms.

lead_in_timeline.summary: After the first trade was closed around breakeven, analysis reset. A reversal candidate appeared near dVAL/dPOC after bearish leverage expansion, followed by a downside sweep and CVD recovery while OI stopped expanding. This taught sweep -> stabilization -> reclaim rather than blind bottom fishing.

The sequence exposed several distinct regimes: Price DOWN + CVD UP + OI DOWN buyer inefficiency; Price UP + CVD DOWN + OI UP leveraged sell absorption; then a breakout above value that failed back below dPOC with OI collapse and long liquidations. Path dependence became mandatory: endpoint matrices alone miss traps.

Large long-liquidation waves taught that liquidation size is not a bottom signal. The strongest new hypothesis became recovery efficiency: if CVD and OI repair strongly but price cannot reclaim broken value, buyer effort is inefficient and a failed-reclaim short can be armed. The missed short was audited and long/short analysis was made symmetric.

The prior failed-reclaim short edge paid off, then OI collapsed with price, showing deleveraging rather than a clean new short build. This reinforced the rule: the edge is at the failed repair, not after the move is already paid.

Headline CPI matched expectations while core CPI MoM was slightly hotter. BTC wicked to 76,030 on the execution chart, creating a macro liquidation event. The correct question became whether bad news would be absorbed or turn into fresh bearish leverage expansion.

Price recovered from the CPI wick and reclaimed dVAL. CVD surged while OI stayed almost flat, a healthier recovery than prior leveraged bounces because aggressive demand was not accompanied by a large fresh leverage build.
The second actual BTC long became visible on the execution screenshot at an average entry of 77,613.3 and size 0.0191 BTC after the reclaim sequence.

eth_confirmation.interpretation: ETH impulsively reclaimed and extended above its 15m MA cluster, confirming broad risk-on follow-through rather than a BTC-only microstructure bounce.

lead_in_timeline.current_interpretation: The long reclaim path is validated so far, but the actual CASE-002 position remains open until explicit closure is confirmed.

case_002_core_lessons_so_far: Do not begin this case at CPI; the setup was built from multiple days of post-CASE-001 observations, audits and failed-reclaim research.
After capitulation, compare price repair with CVD and OI repair. Strong effort with weak structural repair is a short-edge candidate; efficient structural reclaim is a long-edge candidate.
CVD surge + nearly flat OI + structural reclaim is higher-quality long recovery evidence than price rising mainly on rapid leverage expansion.
The short edge and long edge are mirror images: failed repair below value versus accepted reclaim above value.
Cross-asset confirmation from ETH can increase confidence that a BTC move is broad risk-on rather than isolated flow noise.
Raw screenshots are evidence events. Canonical CASE-002 is the entire continuous learning/trade episode, not one screenshot or one news event.
